heard: A postage stamp declaring Pluto unexploded inspired a spacecraft to visit it. In 1991, the Postal Service released a set showing every planet alongside its visitor, except the ninth. Pluto's stamp simply read Pluto, not yet explored. The phrase irked researchers so much that it became a call to arms for a new mission. On January 19, 2006, New Horizons launched as the fastest object ever sent from Earth. A Jupiter gravity assist shaved three years off the voyage, sending the probe speeding toward the solar system. On July 14, 2015, the spacecraft finally completed its historic close flyby of Pluto. Hidden onboard all along was that exact 1991 stamp delivered right to its destination. A postage stamp declaring Pluto unexploded inspired a spacecraft to visit it.
